newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wholesalers' stocks up modestly in May.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wholesalers' stocks up modestly in May.

text.p: Sales by wholesalers picked up in May after two consecutive months of declines, the Commerce Department said on Wednesday, as stocks of goods on hand increased modestly.
Inventories increased 0.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted $258.68 billion in May after a revised 0.5 percent decline in April that previously was reported as a sharper 0.7 percent fall.
Sales rose 0.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted $210.35 billion in May after declines of 0.1 percent in April and 0.8 percent in March.

Wholesalers were left with 1.23 months' worth of goods on hand in May, the same as in March and April. The inventories-to-sales ratio measures how long it would take to deplete existing inventories at the current sales pace.

The slight pickup in May inventories was in line with Wall Street economists' expectations. Analysts said before the report was released that larger inventories might indicate anticipation of stronger consumer spending in the third quarter.
All the inventory rise was concentrated in costly durable goods like cars, lumber and machinery, as stocks of durables grew by 0.5 percent to $165.24 billion following a 0.2 percent gain in April.
By contrast, inventories of more quickly used nondurable products like farm products, chemicals and alcoholic products declined 0.2 percent in May to $93.44 billion after a 1.8 percent drop in April.

On the sales side, the pickup in May business occurred entirely among for nondurable goods, especially drugs, alcohol and groceries as sales increased 1 percent to $102.18 billion after a 1.8 percent decrease in April.
Among durable goods, sales dropped 0.5 percent to $108.17 billion after a 1.4 percent rise in April. The May sales drop was especially sharp for furniture, lumber and professional equipment.
But sales of automotive products, which represent factory deliveries to dealers, were up 1 percent to $18.12 billion in May after a 1.8 percent drop in April.
